title: Expanded-family retained exposure and learning-health audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Retained identity-resolved exposure and scalar health can distinguish absent family exposure or gross update collapse from negative strength evidence.
material_change: Zero-new-hand descriptive audit of eight completed expanded-family trial suffixes; no policy changes or causal inference.

result.summary: All eight immutable training suffixes audited with zero new hands; all seven expanded fixed families received actual transition observations.
result.conclusion: No absent-family exposure or gross scalar update-collapse signature: entropy near0.51, approximate KL near0.0025-0.0031, zero or one KL early stop per branch. Stage2 original-three-anchor observations fell from383733 to188195 for Seed1 and368968 to209891 for Seed3; added four families received270103 and268339 observations. These are transition observations, not physical-deal counts or gradient mass. Expanded training reward increased within each stage2 suffix but changing opponent/state distributions prevent causal interpretation. Lower critic MSE and reference KL did not imply stronger poker.
result.decision: Do not patch optimizer or resume infrastructure from this evidence. Exposure redistribution is real but causality is unproven; determine whether expanded endpoints improved against the newly trained families before choosing weighting repair versus a different learning objective.
result.next_step: Preregister one matched two-seed frozen final-endpoint evaluation on the four added training families using new fixed deals; explicitly label it in-distribution adaptation, not unseen transfer or Slumbot qualification. Compare both arms to their own original parent; no outcome-selected checkpoints or additional stages.
